examShortTricks: Trick 1: One-sided limits first: lim x→a⁻ and lim x→a⁺ must be EQUAL for the limit to exist — check both before answering any piecewise or |x| question.
Trick 2: Geometric meaning: the curve approaches the height L from both sides of x = a (holes allowed); physical: instantaneous behaviour as t → t0.
Trick 3: lim f(x) exists but f(a) undefined/unequal → removable discontinuity (a hole) — naming the type earns the mark.
practiceQuestions: Q. Does lim x→0 |x|/x exist? (2 marks) — left −1, right +1 → does not exist.
Q. Give the geometric interpretation of a limit. (1 mark) — f(x) approaches L as x approaches a from both sides.

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Bank of standards — sin x/x → 1; tan x/x → 1; (1 − cos x)/x² → 1/2; (e^x − 1)/x → 1; ln(1+x)/x → 1; (1+x)^(1/x) → e; (a^x − b^x)/x → ln(a/b).
Trick 2: Force the standard form: whatever the argument (3x, 5x²), rewrite so the inner expression matches the standard's variable — e.g. sin 5x/5x → 1, then rescale.
Trick 3: ∞ forms: divide numerator and denominator by the highest power of x; the leading coefficients give the answer.
Trick 4: 1^∞ forms: take log — lim f^g = e^(lim g(f − 1)) when f → 1.
practiceQuestions: Q. Evaluate lim x→0 (sin 3x)/x. (1 mark) — 3.
Q. Evaluate lim x→0 (5^x − 3^x)/x. (2 marks) — ln(5/3).
Q. Evaluate lim x→∞ (3x² + 2x)/(x² + 1). (1 mark) — 3.

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Instant classifications: polynomials, sin/cos, e^x continuous everywhere; tan x, sec x break at π/2 + nπ; ln x only for x > 0; |x| continuous but not differentiable at 0.
Trick 2: Sums/products/quotients of continuous functions are continuous except where the denominator vanishes — locate the bad points, not the whole curve.
Trick 3: For an unknown constant k in a piecewise function, write the continuity equation lim-left = lim-right (and = f(a)) and solve for k.
practiceQuestions: Q. Where is f(x) = 1/(x² − 4) discontinuous? (1 mark) — x = ±2 (denominator zero).
Q. Find k if f(x) = kx + 1 (x ≤ 2), 3x − 1 (x > 2) is continuous. (2 marks) — 2k + 1 = 5 → k = 2.

examShortTricks: Trick 1: The relation in one arrow: differentiable ⇒ continuous; continuous ⇏ differentiable — counterexample |x| at 0 is the standard proof line.
Trick 2: Differentiability test: LHD = RHD (both limits of the difference quotient); unequal or infinite → not differentiable at that point.
Trick 3: Sharp corners, cusps, vertical tangents kill differentiability — |x|, x^(2/3), 1/x-type points are the standard examples.
practiceQuestions: Q. Show that f(x) = |x| is continuous but not differentiable at 0. (3 marks) — LHD = −1, RHD = +1 → not differentiable; both one-sided limits equal 0 → continuous.
Q. If a function is differentiable at a, what follows? (1 mark) — it is continuous there.

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Inverse-trig derivatives are the exam core: d(sin^-1 u) = u′/√(1−u²); d(tan^-1 u) = u′/(1+u²); d(sec^-1 u) = u′/(|u|√(u²−1)).
Trick 2: Logarithmic differentiation for f(x)^{g(x)}: take ln both sides, differentiate, multiply back — works for x^x, x^(sin x).
Trick 3: Simplify BEFORE differentiating: expand products, split fractions, apply log laws — half the algebra work disappears.
Trick 4: Chain-rule discipline: differentiate the outer function first, multiply by the derivative of the inner — write the layers explicitly for long composites.
practiceQuestions: Q. Differentiate tan^-1(2x). (1 mark) — 2/(1 + 4x²).
Q. Differentiate x^(sin x). (2 marks) — x^(sin x)[cos x · ln x + sin x/x].
Q. Differentiate e^(3x) sin 2x. (2 marks) — e^(3x)(3 sin 2x + 2 cos 2x).

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Formula: (uv)_n = u_n v + nC1 u_{n−1} v1 + … + u v_n — binomial pattern with derivatives of u descending and of v ascending.
Trick 2: Choose u = the factor that becomes zero after a few derivatives (polynomial like x²) and v = the repeating one (e^{ax}, sin bx) — the work collapses.
Trick 3: nth-derivative bank: (e^{ax})_n = a^n e^{ax}; (sin(ax+b))_n = a^n sin(ax + b + nπ/2); (1/(x+a))_n = (−1)^n n!/(x+a)^{n+1} — quote, don't recompute.
Trick 4: For y = e^{ax}x², write (uv)_n with u = x² (only 3 nonzero terms) — the standard exam example.
practiceQuestions: Q. Find the nth derivative of x² e^{3x}. (4 marks) — 3^n e^{3x}(x² + 2nx/3 + n(n−1)/9).
Q. nth derivative of sin 2x. (1 mark) — 2^n sin(2x + nπ/2).

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Slope pack: m_tangent = dy/dx at the point; m_normal = −1/(dy/dx) — then point-slope form finishes the line.
Trick 2: Tangent parallel to x-axis → dy/dx = 0; parallel to y-axis → dx/dy = 0 — the two special cases are the standard 2-markers.
Trick 3: For implicit curves, find dy/dx by implicit differentiation, substitute the given point, then build both lines — never solve for y explicitly.
Trick 4: Tangent length and subtangent questions: use y = m(x − x1) + y1 and intercepts with the axes.
practiceQuestions: Q. Find the tangent and normal to y = x² at (1, 1). (3 marks) — tangent slope 2: y = 2x − 1; normal slope −1/2: x + 2y = 3.
Q. Where is the tangent to y = x³ − 3x horizontal? (1 mark) — x = ±1 (dy/dx = 3x² − 3 = 0).

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Monotonicity: solve f′ > 0 (increasing) and f′ < 0 (decreasing) as INEQUALITIES on the domain — answer with intervals.
Trick 2: Second-derivative test: at f′ = 0 point, f″ > 0 → minimum; f″ < 0 → maximum; f″ = 0 → inconclusive, use a sign chart.
Trick 3: Word-problem protocol: model the quantity in one variable → domain → differentiate → critical points → verify type → answer with units and a sentence.
Trick 4: Absolute vs local: compare f at all critical points AND the endpoints for a closed interval — forgetting endpoints is the classic lost mark.
practiceQuestions: Q. Find the local extrema of f(x) = x³ − 6x² + 9x. (4 marks) — f′ = 3(x−1)(x−3); max at 1 (4), min at 3 (0).
Q. Find the intervals where f(x) = x + 1/x increases. (2 marks) — |x| > 1; decreases on (−1, 0) ∪ (0, 1).
Q. Minimum of x + 1/x for x > 0? (1 mark) — 2 at x = 1 (AM–GM or calculus).

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Related rates recipe: write the relation between variables → differentiate w.r.t. t → substitute known values and rates → solve; keep units in the final answer.
Trick 2: Approximation: f(x + δx) ≈ f(x) + f′(x)δx — choose the base point where f and f′ are easy (e.g. 25 for √26).
Trick 3: Relative error = δx/x; percentage error ×100 — for products, relative errors ADD: δ(P)/P = δa/a + δb/b.
Trick 4: For sphere/volume rates, differentiate V = (4/3)πr³ → dV/dt = 4πr² dr/dt — quote the differentiated form first for the method mark.
practiceQuestions: Q. A cube's edge grows at 3 cm/s; find the rate of increase of volume when the edge is 10 cm. (3 marks) — dV/dt = 3a²·da/dt = 900 cm³/s.
Q. Approximate √26. (2 marks) — √25 + 1/(2·5) = 5.1.
Q. If the radius of a circle has 2% error, the area error is? (1 mark) — 4% (errors double for squares).

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Method picker — rational with factorable denominator → partial fractions; product of unlike types → by parts; composite f(g(x))g′(x) → substitution; roots of quadratics → complete the square.
Trick 2: By parts ILATE: pick u = the factor that simplifies on differentiation (log, inverse trig first); ∫u dv = uv − ∫v du.
Trick 3: Partial fraction forms: (px+q)/((x−a)(x−b)) = A/(x−a) + B/(x−b); repeated factor adds B/(x−a)²; irreducible quadratic adds (Cx+D)/(x²+px+q).
Trick 4: Standard definite-integral properties save work: ∫0^a f(x)dx = ∫0^a f(a−x)dx — apply to sin/cos symmetric integrands.
practiceQuestions: Q. Evaluate ∫ x ln x dx. (2 marks) — (x²/2)ln x − x²/4 + C.
Q. Integrate 1/((x+1)(x+2)). (2 marks) — ln|(x+1)/(x+2)| + C.
Q. Evaluate ∫0^{π/2} sin x/(sin x + cos x) dx. (2 marks) — π/4 by the f(x) ↔ f(a−x) property.

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Classifier — can you write g(y)dy = f(x)dx? → variable separable; M dx + N dy with M, N homogeneous of same degree → put y = vx; dy/dx + Py = Q → linear (integrating factor e^{∫P dx}).
Trick 2: Linear equation answer template: y·IF = ∫Q·IF dx + C — write it immediately after finding the IF.
Trick 3: For homogeneous equations, the substitution y = vx ALWAYS ends in a separable equation; back-substitute v = y/x at the end.
Trick 4: Initial conditions determine C — substitute the point BEFORE simplifying the general solution to avoid algebra errors.
practiceQuestions: Q. Solve dy/dx = xy. (2 marks) — ln y = x²/2 + C → y = Ce^{x²/2}.
Q. Solve dy/dx + y/x = x². (3 marks) — IF = x; yx = x⁴/4 + C.
Q. Solve dy/dx = (y + x)/(y − x). (3 marks) — y = vx → x dv/dx = (1+v²)/(1−v)... integrate: ln(x√(1+v²))... final implicit answer.
